source: OrbitStudio travel list (orbitstudio3d.com), via the OrbitStudio connector, 2026-10-28

landmarks.name: Alba Mons
landmarks.description: Alba Mons is a very broad, low volcano north of the Tharsis volcanoes, about 548 km across in the IAU Gazetteer; its lava flows spread much further.

landmarks.name: Arsia Mons
landmarks.description: Arsia Mons is a shield volcano about 470 km across, the southernmost of the three Tharsis Montes, with a large summit caldera.

landmarks.name: Ascraeus Mons
landmarks.description: Ascraeus Mons is a shield volcano about 456 km across, the northernmost of the three Tharsis Montes.

landmarks.name: Elysium Mons
landmarks.description: Elysium Mons is a shield volcano about 401 km across, the main volcano of the Elysium volcanic region.

landmarks.name: Olympus Mons
landmarks.description: Olympus Mons' summit is 21,290 m above the Mars datum, about 22,000 m above the plains at its base. It is 600 km wide, at 18.65° N, 133.80° W.

landmarks.name: Pavonis Mons
landmarks.description: Pavonis Mons is a shield volcano about 366 km across, the middle one of the three Tharsis Montes, sitting almost on the equator.

landmarks.name: Candor Chasma
landmarks.description: Candor Chasma is a canyon about 811 km long in the central part of Valles Marineris, north of Melas Chasma.

landmarks.name: Hebes Chasma
landmarks.description: Hebes Chasma is an enclosed canyon about 317 km long north of the main Valles Marineris system, with a large mesa in its middle.

landmarks.name: Melas Chasma
landmarks.description: Melas Chasma is a canyon about 564 km long in the middle of Valles Marineris, one of the widest parts of the system.

landmarks.name: Noctis Labyrinthus
landmarks.description: Noctis Labyrinthus is a maze of intersecting troughs about 1,190 km across at the western end of Valles Marineris.

landmarks.name: Valles Marineris
landmarks.description: Valles Marineris is about 4,000 km long, up to 600 km wide and 11 km deep below the plateau, centred at 14.01° S, 58.59° W on Mars.

landmarks.name: Endeavour Crater
landmarks.description: Endeavour is an impact crater about 22 km across in Meridiani Planum; the Opportunity rover explored its rim from 2011 until the end of its mission in 2018.

landmarks.name: Gale Crater
landmarks.description: Gale Crater is 154 km across, with Mount Sharp at its center — Curiosity's crater.

landmarks.name: Gusev Crater
landmarks.description: Gusev is an impact crater about 158 km across where the Spirit rover landed in 2004. Named after the Russian astronomer Matvei Gusev.

landmarks.name: Huygens Crater
landmarks.description: Huygens is a large impact crater about 467 km across in the southern highlands. Named after the Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens.

landmarks.name: Jezero Crater
landmarks.description: Jezero Crater is 45 km across and once held a lake — Perseverance's crater, with its river delta.

landmarks.name: Korolev Crater
landmarks.description: Korolev is an impact crater about 81 km across near the north pole, filled with a mound of water ice all year round. Named after the Soviet rocket engineer Sergei Korolev.

landmarks.name: Lomonosov Crater
landmarks.description: Lomonosov is an impact crater about 130 km across in the northern plains. Named after the Russian scientist Mikhail Lomonosov.

landmarks.name: Schiaparelli Crater
landmarks.description: Schiaparelli is a large impact crater about 458 km across near the equator. Named after the Italian astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli.

landmarks.name: Ares Vallis
landmarks.description: Ares Vallis is an outflow channel about 1,760 km long carved by ancient floods; Mars Pathfinder landed near its mouth in 1997.

landmarks.name: Cerberus Fossae
landmarks.description: Cerberus Fossae is a set of young fissures about 1,240 km long in Elysium Planitia, the source of many of the marsquakes InSight recorded.

landmarks.name: Kasei Valles
landmarks.description: Kasei Valles is one of the largest outflow channel systems on Mars, about 1,580 km long, draining into Chryse Planitia.

landmarks.name: Mawrth Vallis
landmarks.description: Mawrth Vallis is an ancient channel about 635 km long, known for its layered, clay-rich rocks.

landmarks.name: Nili Fossae
landmarks.description: Nili Fossae is a set of long troughs about 728 km long on the north-western rim of the Isidis basin, near Jezero crater.

landmarks.name: Argyre Planitia
landmarks.description: Argyre Planitia is a plain about 893 km across on the floor of the Argyre impact basin in the southern highlands.

landmarks.name: Chryse Planitia
landmarks.description: Chryse Planitia is a smooth plain about 1,540 km across where large outflow channels end; Viking 1 landed on it in 1976.

landmarks.name: Elysium Planitia
landmarks.description: Elysium Planitia is a broad plain about 3,000 km across near the equator; the InSight lander set down on it in 2018.

landmarks.name: Hellas Planitia
landmarks.description: Hellas Planitia is the plain on the floor of the Hellas impact basin, about 2,300 km across and nearly 9 km deep, one of the largest impact basins in the Solar System.

landmarks.name: Isidis Planitia
landmarks.description: Isidis Planitia is a plain about 1,220 km across inside an ancient impact basin; Beagle 2 landed on it in 2003.

landmarks.name: Meridiani Planum
landmarks.description: Meridiani Planum is a plain about 1,060 km across on the equator where the Opportunity rover landed in 2004 and found evidence of water in the planet's past.

landmarks.name: Syrtis Major Planum
landmarks.description: Syrtis Major Planum is a dark volcanic plain about 1,210 km across, the first surface feature recorded on another planet (Christiaan Huygens drew it in 1659).

landmarks.name: Utopia Planitia
landmarks.description: Utopia Planitia is a vast plain about 3,560 km across in the northern lowlands, inside a huge impact basin; Viking 2 landed on it in 1976 and China's Zhurong rover in 2021.

landmarks.name: Planum Australe
landmarks.description: Planum Australe is the plateau of layered ice and dust around Mars's south pole, topped by a cap of frozen carbon dioxide.

landmarks.name: Planum Boreum
landmarks.description: Planum Boreum is the plateau of layered water ice and dust around Mars's north pole.

landmarks.name: Beagle 2
landmarks.description: The British Beagle 2 lander, carried by ESA's Mars Express, landed here in Isidis Planitia on 25 December 2003 and was never heard from; HiRISE images found it in 2015 with its solar panels only partly opened.

landmarks.name: Curiosity
landmarks.description: NASA's Curiosity rover landed here in Gale crater on 6 August 2012 (UTC), near Mount Sharp, the mound in the crater's center.

landmarks.name: InSight
landmarks.description: NASA's InSight lander set down here in western Elysium Planitia on 26 November 2018 to study the planet's interior and record marsquakes.

landmarks.name: Opportunity
landmarks.description: NASA's Opportunity rover landed here in Meridiani Planum, inside the small Eagle crater, on 25 January 2004 (UTC).

landmarks.name: Pathfinder
landmarks.description: NASA's Mars Pathfinder landed here in Ares Vallis on 4 July 1997 and released Sojourner, the first rover on Mars.

landmarks.name: Perseverance
landmarks.description: NASA's Perseverance rover landed here in Jezero crater on 18 February 2021, carrying the Ingenuity helicopter.

landmarks.name: Phoenix
landmarks.description: NASA's Phoenix lander set down here in Vastitas Borealis, the northern plains at about 68 degrees north, on 25 May 2008 (UTC).

landmarks.name: Spirit
landmarks.description: NASA's Spirit rover landed here in Gusev crater on 4 January 2004 (UTC).

landmarks.name: Viking 1
landmarks.description: NASA's Viking 1 lander set down here in western Chryse Planitia on 20 July 1976, the first successful US landing on Mars.

landmarks.name: Viking 2
landmarks.description: NASA's Viking 2 lander set down here in Utopia Planitia on 3 September 1976.

landmarks.name: Zhurong
landmarks.description: China's Zhurong rover, part of the Tianwen-1 mission, landed here in southern Utopia Planitia on 14 May 2021 (UTC).
